**Decided; do not reopen.**
- Store: SQLite, WAL, `<SPUD_HOME>/.spud/ledger.db`. Per connection: `foreign_keys = ON`, `busy_timeout = 5000`, `synchronous = NORMAL`. Every write is `BEGIN IMMEDIATE … COMMIT`, short, holding nothing else. One connection per process. Reads run outside write transactions. Backup is `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` then `VACUUM INTO .spud/backups/ledger-<stamp>.db`.
- `SPUD_HOME` resolution: the env var; else the git common dir of `bin/spud`'s real path (`Path(__file__).resolve()`, `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`); else `~/.config/spud/home`. Tests set `SPUD_HOME` to a temp dir.
- Schema: the spike's DDL, `STRICT`, with these amendments, each listed again in your Result as a written difference: (a) per-project prefixes: `projects.ticket_prefix`, `projects.team_prefix`, `tickets.number INTEGER NOT NULL`, `UNIQUE (project_id, number)`, `tickets.id` a plain surrogate, `key = ticket_prefix || '-' || printf('%03d', number)` and `team_key` likewise, the counter `max(number) + 1` per project inside the insert transaction; `spud.config.json`'s `tickets.prefix` and `teams.prefix` are the home project's values, written by `config sync`; (b) fan-out limits count children with `status IN ('planned','active')` under the parent, lineage numbers count every child ever planned; (c) the generated-file marker `<!-- generated by spud from .spud/ledger.db; edit with the spud CLI -->` goes immediately after the closing `---` of the frontmatter, never before it, because Obsidian reads properties only from a frontmatter block at byte 0; (d) anything else you must change, with the reason.
- Migrations: `PRAGMA user_version`, numbered SQL strings embedded in the file, forward only, `VACUUM INTO` backup before each; `init` is idempotent: create if absent, migrate if behind, refuse if ahead. Views and triggers dropped and recreated by every migration.
- Config: `spud.config.json` is read on every invocation for the limits (the config wins). `config sync` mirrors `naming.pool` into `name_pool` and the home project's prefixes. `settings sync` generates `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` and `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` in a `.claude/settings.json` from `limits`, preserving every other key; it takes `--path` and `--dry-run`; tests run it against a temp copy only. Never run it against this repo.
- Ownership: `--as spud | <agent_id> | SPUD-nnn/<Name>`; column ownership per the spike's matrix; a write outside the actor's columns is refused with a reason on stderr and a distinct exit code. Until [[SPD-008]] installs hooks, `--as SPUD-nnn/<Name>` is trusted by prose; say so in `--help`.
- Timestamps come from the clock only, stored ISO 8601 with seconds and local offset; rendered as the committed files have them (`created: YYYY-MM-DD`, `spawned: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`, `finished: ""` when null). Imported timestamps keep what the file said; each imported row gets an `import` event with the source path.
- Events: append-only, both triggers; every mutation writes one; event kinds as the spike lists them.
- Render: each generated file written whole via temp file and `rename`; the `renders` table keeps the SHA-256; a file on disk whose hash differs from the record is a hand edit: refuse that file, write a `render` event with `data.conflict = true`, print the path; `import --file <path>` accepts the edit; `render --out <dir>` renders to another directory for the acceptance test. `Home.md`, `Spud.md`, the `.base` files and `_templates/` are never generated.
- Reports: import each `## HH:MM — title` entry of `reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md` as one `report.entry` event (body verbatim, `at` from the date and heading time); render the day file from its events; `report add` appends one entry with the clock time, a title and Spud's Next line. Automatic lines are [[SPD-011]].
- `card` prints a ticket's team tree (name, id, persona, model, status, spawned, finished, summary when present); the rendered `## Team` section keeps today's nested list form ([[SPD-010]] redesigns it). `board` and `fleet` print tables from `v_board` and `v_fleet`, with `board --brief` for [[SPD-011]]. `doctor` prints interpreter path and version, SQLite library version, `SPUD_HOME`, database path, `user_version`, journal mode, the three pragmas, and config sanity (unique pool names, integer limits), nonzero on a problem. Every command takes `--json`.
- State machines: tickets `queued → active → done`, `queued → declined`, `active → queued`; members `planned → active → done | blocked | failed`, `planned → failed`. `member new` inserts the `planned` row after the depth, fan-out and concurrency checks inside the same `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, draws the lineage and a random unused name from `name_pool` unless `--name` is given, requires `--tier-reason` when the model is not the persona's default. `member log|result|block` are the member's. `member finish --status … --outcome … [--summary …]` is the parent's and stamps `finished_at`. `proposal file` is the member's; `proposal decide --decision absorb|decline|escalate|create` records a `proposal_decisions` row, and `create` makes a ticket with `origin = 'proposal'`. `handoff add` records a handoff. `ticket new|move|edit|show`.

**Acceptance test** (`tests/test_acceptance.py`): extract `git archive HEAD ledger reports` into a temp dir (read-only git; it keeps in-flight files such as your own out of the corpus), `spud init` with a temp `SPUD_HOME`, `spud import <tmp>/ledger <tmp>/reports`, `spud render --out <tmp>/out`, then compare every generated file with its source: frontmatter keys and values identical, the same sections in the same order with identical content, wikilinks identical. Allowed differences: the marker line, trailing whitespace, runs of blank lines. Print a unified diff on failure. Add unit tests for: the limit checks (fan-out alive-at-once frees a slot when a child finishes; depth; concurrency), lineage numbering across finished children, the name draw, ownership refusals, both state machines, append-only events, the hand-edit conflict and `import --file`, per-project counters and keys, idempotent `init`, `settings sync` on a temp settings file, and a concurrency smoke test with a handful of processes writing at once with zero `database is locked` errors.

**Team.** You may have up to 2 sub-agents alive at once; depth remaining below you is 1, so each gets "no sub-agents". Recommended shape: write the CLI yourself (one file, one author; never let two agents edit `bin/spud`). When the acceptance test passes, spawn a reviewer on fable as `01.01` to check `bin/spud` against this brief and the spike: run the tests independently, read the DDL against the spike's, try to break ownership, limits and the render conflict, and report in its Result. Fix what it finds, record its Outcome. A scout on haiku is fine for a lookup. Use the superpowers test-driven-development and systematic-debugging skills; this ticket creates the repo's first test suite.

**Done when.** `python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests` passes and your Result quotes the run; the acceptance diff is formatting-only; `spud doctor` reports the interpreter and SQLite version; every DDL difference from the spike is listed in your Result with its reason; `git status` shows only `bin/spud`, `tests/` and `ledger/teams/SPUD-007/`; no `.spud/` exists in this repo; nothing is cut over.

Per Eric's decision 2 (per-project prefixes): `projects.ticket_prefix` and `projects.team_prefix` (both `UNIQUE`, which is how the importer resolves a project from a file's prefix); `tickets.number INTEGER NOT NULL` with `UNIQUE (project_id, number)`; `tickets.id` a plain surrogate; `key` and `team_key` computed by the CLI as `<prefix>-%03d` from `max(number) + 1` per project inside the insert transaction. `spud.config.json`'s `tickets.prefix` and `teams.prefix` are the home project's values, written by `init` and `config sync`.
2. Per decision 3 (fan-out counts children alive at once): a query change only, `count(*) … WHERE parent_id IS ? AND status IN ('planned','active')`; the spike's `members_live` index serves it. Lineage numbering counts every child ever planned.
3. `tickets.heading TEXT`: SPD-003, SPD-005 and SPD-006 shorten their H1 against `title`; NULL means the title.
4. `tickets.layout` and `members.layout` (JSON, NULL = the template): the committed files vary in frontmatter key presence and order (`proposed_by` is absent on SPD-001, SPD-004 and SPD-005 and empty on SPD-006) and in section order (Dakota carries an extra `## Sources`); the render reproduces the file's layout, new rows get the template's.
5. Table `imported_sections (entity, entity_id, section, body, through_id)`: markdown-v0 prose the rows cannot regenerate (annotations after the tuple on Team and Sub-agents lines, template comment lines, free-form `## Ticket proposals`, list preambles, `## Sources`), stored only where the rows-only render differs from the file (32 of the corpus's sections, pinned by the acceptance test), with a per-section watermark so rows the CLI adds later render after the prose. 6. `renders.content TEXT`: the text last written, so `import --file` is a three-way accept (file against the last render; only the delta is an edit) and never reverts a change the CLI made since the render.
7. The `events.kind` CHECK adds `member.edited` (brief, deliverables, model, summary edited after planning) and `config.synced` (`config sync` is a mutation, and every mutation writes an event).

**Deviations from the brief's letter, each decided by Spud on Annabelle's review or on my questions.** The member machine is `planned → active → done | blocked | failed`, `planned → failed`, and `blocked → active` (`member start` after a re-brief, parent-owned, clears `finished`; a re-spawn is a new row). `member start` (planned → active, stamping `spawned_at` from the clock) is the parent's until SPD-008's hooks make the transition from `PostToolUse(Agent)`. Parent-owned columns (`status`, `outcome`, `summary`, `finished_at`, `brief`, `deliverables`, `model`) may be written by the direct parent or any ancestor, Spud included, so a grandchild can still be recorded when its lead dies (Law 9). `member new` requires a non-empty `--brief` (the ledger never holds a briefless member); `member edit --brief` is the re-brief. `handoff add` refuses Spud → Spud (both parties NULL marks an imported line kept whole). `proposal decide`: Spud may `create` or `decline`; a member may `absorb`, `decline` or `escalate`; `create` by a member is refused with exit 3 (Law 6). A member planning on another ticket, or recording a handoff on a ticket it is not on, is refused with exit 3. Imported rows invent no timestamp: `closed_at` stays NULL; `updated_at`, `planned_at`, `filed_at` and the import-time decision's `at` take the file's one date and the row's `import` event names them under `data.derived`. Hand edits (Eric's decision 4, read narrowly): `import --file` is Spud's (`--as spud`); it accepts a ticket's title, priority, tags, status (through the state machine, with the stamps and the event), Brief, Size and Outcome, a member's Brief, Outcome and status (through the machine), and an appended report entry; everything else is refused with the command that changes it, and `render --discard <path>` (Spud's) puts a refused or unwanted hand edit back to the render, keeping the discarded text in the `render` event. `~/.config/spud/home` is read as the third fallback but never written (SPD-014 writes it).

**Left.** Cutover is Eric's go, not this ticket; Law 10 (commit 2f11506) means Spud moves `bin/` and `tests/` onto a worktree branch at my return. Out of scope, noted for SPD-008 or later (Annabelle's note 13): nothing stops a finished member from `member log|result` or `proposal file`, a parent from finishing while its children are alive, or a ticket from closing with alive members; `render`, `config sync` and `backup` take no actor. Also for later: `--version` and argparse usage errors are not JSON under `--json`; `settings sync` normalises a settings file's indentation to 2; the importer parses `## Ticket proposals` only as prose (it is the one-time migration tool the spike describes, not a two-way sync).
